newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey sees Iraq pipeline in operation this week.
newsitem.headline: Turkey sees Iraq pipeline in operation this week.

text.p: A Turkish Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Monday he expects the Iraq-Turkey pipeline to be in operation this week for Iraqi oil exports under the U.N. oil-for-food plan, the state-run Anatolian news agency reported.
"We expect the pipeline to go into operation very soon, during this week," ministry spokesman Omer Akbel told reporters at a news briefing.
U.N. officials said at the weekend Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali was ready to give the go-ahead for the oil-for-food deal on Monday, barring last minute obstacles.
Akbel said a ceremony would be held at Turkey's southern Ceyhan port to commemorate the reopening of the pipeline, but did not say when the ceremony would take place or who would take part.
The 986-km (616-mile) twin pipeline from Iraq's Kirkuk oilfields to Ceyhan has remained idle since the U.N. trade embargo on Iraq after it invaded Iraq in 1990.
